subject: Post-demo: telemetry & sensitive-data controls — clarification + next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: telemetry & sensitive-data controls — clarification + next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying questions so we can scope an accurate proposal and technical workbook for your security team.

What I heard from the call (high level):
- Hemlock needs guarantee that PII is not persisted in plain text in any persistent request/response logs or event telemetry.
- Retention for audit logs and traces should be limited to 30 days and must be stored in the EU (eu-west region).
- You ideally want field-level redaction that can be configured by Hemlock (rule-based), and visibility into what was redacted for audit purposes.
- Headers / trace IDs: you want to ensure trace IDs are either hashed/mapped or excluded from logs to prevent correlation with internal IDs.

Questions to confirm (please answer inline):
1) Is the retention requirement a strict 30-day window with automated deletion after day 30, or is a longer retention with admin-triggered deletion acceptable?
2) For redaction: do you require client-controlled regex/field lists (i.e., Hemlock provides a manifest of sensitive keys), or would a Redwood-managed set plus allowlist be acceptable?
3) For headers & trace IDs: do you want any correlation IDs preserved in a hashed form for debugging, or must all request-level identifiers be scrubbed entirely?
4) Are there any compliance artifacts (SAML assertions, specific headers) you need us to redact from traces? If so, can you share examples or field names (we can treat those as sensitive during the PoC).

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll attach a short one-pager describing: logging levels, what we persist by default, and the redaction options (inline rules vs. pre-send scrubbing).
- If answers above are straightforward, schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive next week with our infra/engineering team to map exact config for the PoC (I recommend including a security owner from Hemlock).
- We can prepare a scoped PoC that demonstrates: EU-only retention, automated 30-day deletion, and a sample redaction policy applied to a small traffic set.

Attachments: Redwood-Logging-Controls-OnePager.pdf (summary + config examples).

Thanks — I’ll block time for a follow-up once I get your availability.

—
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Post-demo: telemetry & sensitive-data controls — clarification + next steps

Thanks Karthik — high level answers below. I’m copying our security mailbox for any deeper questions.

Answers:
1) Retention: 30 days is our baseline requirement. We can consider up to 90 days if we can enforce encryption-at-rest in EU and have an automatic purge policy at 30 days for production logs. For the PoC please implement strict 30-day deletion.
2) Redaction: we need customer-controlled rules. Hemlock will provide a list of sensitive field names and some regex examples (SSN formats, account numbers). We want the ability in the console to toggle rules on/off per environment.
3) Trace IDs: prefer hashed correlation IDs that are reversible only with a Hemlock-owned key (i.e., we can map for debugging but Redwood can’t reverse without our key). If that isn’t possible, exclude trace IDs from logs entirely.
4) Example headers: we send SAML assertions and an internal X-Hemlock-Session header. Those must not appear in persistent logs. I’ll follow up with a sample header dump by EOD.

Also: what is the default retention for request payloads and response bodies in hosted mode? Are request/response bodies persisted by default or only accessible transiently for live debugging?

—Alex
Alex Martin
Head of Platform Security | Hemlock Financial
alex.martin@hemlockfinancial.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: telemetry & sensitive-data controls — clarification + next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the quick answers and for confirming the headers you’ll share. Quick clarifications on our side so Hemlock can decide between hosted vs. private deployment for the PoC: 

Default behavior (hosted API):
- Request/response bodies: by default Redwood does not persist full request/response bodies in long-term logs for hosted tenants. Short-term traces are kept for troubleshooting and auto-rotate within 48 hours unless explicitly enabled for retention.
- Request/response logs: structured request/response metadata (status codes, latencies, model variant) are retained for 90 days by default but can be configured down to 0 days; we can enforce a 30-day retention for your account and limit storage to eu-west.
- Headers & trace IDs: headers are captured in structured metadata for routing and debugging; we can configure header scrubbing rules before persistence. Trace IDs can be stored as HMAC-hashed values using a customer-provided key in Dedicated/Private mode; in hosted mode we offer hashed-with-tenant-salt which is not reversible externally.

Options for Hemlock (recommended path):
1) Hosted PoC with strict 30-day, EU-only storage + configurable header/field redaction (Hemlock-provided rule set). For trace ID reversibility you’ll need Dedicated or Private where we can integrate with your KMS to wrap keys.
2) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem): full control — you manage KMS and reversible mapping for trace IDs. This is the cleanest way to meet your hashed-but-reversible requirement.

Next steps I propose:
- Please share the sample header dump (as discussed). We’ll run it through our rule simulator and return a redaction report showing what would be removed/masked.
- If PoC -> we’ll provision a scoped tenant in eu-west with 30-day automated purge and console toggles for field rules.
- Scheduling: I can arrange a 45-min technical session on Tue 2026-05-05 10:00-10:45 PT or Wed 2026-05-06 14:00-14:45 PT. Which works for your security team?

I’ll also attach the one-pager and a short checklist for the PoC so Marissa and Rishi can prep internally.

—
